summary: Early-morning 5xx wave: API gateway accept-queue rollback causing upstream runtime overload for Acme Analytics
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 08:12 UTC Acme Analytics (dedicated tenant) observed a sudden jump in 5xx responses from the Redwood API. Error rate peaked for ~22 minutes with sustained 5xx floor ~8% for their tenant. Impact: Production inference calls returned 502/503 intermittently, downstream application latency spiked and 2 customer workflows timed out. Environment: prod-us-east dedicated pool with pinned model redwood/gptq-13b-v2.

Observed behavior: API gateway began returning 502s while upstream serving-runtime processes remained healthy on basic liveness checks. We observed accept-queue rollbacks on the gateway (connections accepted then immediately closed) correlated with a surge of long-running streaming sessions + prefetch requests from the tenant. That pattern caused sudden backlog on runtime request queue, triggering internal watchdogs and runtime connection churn.

Impact summary: Tenant-visible 5xx, elevated latency, transient drops in throughput, customer reported failed batches and increased error logs in their app.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Tenant issues a high-concurrency burst of streaming + prefetch calls (observed from customer traffic pattern). 2) Gateway accept queue hits transient limit and performs an accept-queue rollback (early-accept close) under current tuning. 3) Upstream runtimes receive high short-lived connection churn, KV cache prefetches spike, and internal request queue waits increase leading to watchdog-triggered restarts. 4) API gateway surfaces 502/503 to callers.

Note: Reproducible in canary with synthetic traffic generator using 1200 concurrent streams + prefetches with long prompt prefixes (>=6k tokens).

investigation_notes: 08:15 UTC: Triage - SRE confirmed spike correlates with tenant connection pattern. No infra-wide outage detected; impact scoped to dedicated pool used by Acme Analytics.
08:18 UTC: Observability - request_queue latency on several runtime replicas jumped >10s; kernel-level metrics showed ephemeral socket churn and increased epoll wait counts.

08:22 UTC: Hypothesis - gateway accept-queue rollback is shedding accepted connections under ephemeral overload, which amplifies upstream churn when many clients reconnect quickly (retry amplification).

08:30 UTC: Reproduction - Ran synthetic load against a dedicated canary pool; reproduced accept-queue rollback when concurrent accepted-but-not-fully-handshook connections exceeded 480-512 threshold under current kernel tunings.

08:45 UTC: Correlation - KV prefetch rate from the tenant increased by 6x during the burst; prefetches are prioritized and generated many long-lived backend handling slots causing head-of-line blocking.
09:05 UTC: Confirmed mitigations - increased apigw accept-queue limit and enabled graceful accept-backpressure handling patch on edge (PR referenced).
comments: Taylor Chen (Support): Customer reported 5xx beginning 08:12 UTC, provided sample request IDs and timestamps. Raised to SRE for investigation.
SRE (Javier Morales): Observed accept-queue rollbacks on edge; temporary mitigation suggested: widen accept backlog and throttle prefetch from tenant via per-tenant rate-limiter.
Aisha Patel (Eng): Deployed temporary apigw tunables at 08:40 UTC (increase backlog to 1024, extend accept timeout). Error rate dropped by ~85% within 3 minutes.
Customer (Acme): Confirmed service restored; reported successful replay of failed requests after 08:50 UTC. Asked for follow-up to prevent recurrence during business-hour spikes.
Security (Nina Rao): Requested review of websocket/keepalive config changes for compatibility with customer L4 proxies (no obvious issues).
root_cause: A confluence of tenant-driven high concurrency (mix of streaming and KV prefetch) and conservative API gateway accept-queue tuning. The gateway's accept-queue rollback behavior caused short-lived connection closures and reconnection churn, which overloaded serving-runtime request queues and triggered watchdog restarts, leading to elevated 5xx rates.
resolution_summary: Short-term: Increased API gateway accept backlog and accept timeout; applied per-tenant soft-throttling on aggressive prefetch endpoints for the Acme dedicated pool. Deployed a hotfix to change accept-queue rollback to a graceful backpressure reply (503 with Retry-After) on edge for overflow conditions. Long-term: Scheduled kernel-level tuning and edge backlog policy change, and a dedicated rate-limiter for prefetch requests outlined in follow-ups. Customer notified and confirmed restoration.
